name: Israel & the Israel of God
about: Who Israel is, the church, and Zionism.

teachings.title: Circumcise your hearts, O Jerusalem
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God called Judah to repent with a circumcision of the heart by faith rather than of the flesh, but they were a stiff-necked people whose destruction was their own doing.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4, and the Spirit of the Lord is upon Jeremiah, preaching to the people of Judah, the children of Israel, and warning them of destruction coming from the North, the lion of Babylon. God giving the prophet visions of an invasion, all the whole the supposed prophets of the Lord are preaching "peace, peace." (As we will see in a later chapter, they are falsely telling Judah that they are fine and God loves them, but they aren't speaking for God).

The Lord tells the people to repent towards Him and He will stay His judgment. To the circumcision of the heart. Not of the flesh, the outward sign of being of the seed of Abraham, but the circumcision made without hands, of faith in the Lord.

**Romans 2:25-29**
*For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision. Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision? And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law? For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*

**Colossians 2:11**
 *In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:*

Even as God is warning of utter destruction and the desolation of her cities, being spoiled by these invading armies, carried away into captivity, justified in His wrath, God offers His grace that if they but turn back to Him, He will repent.

*O Jerusalem, wash thine heart from wickedness, that thou mayest be saved. How long shall thy vain thoughts lodge within thee?*

We can hear in this the frustration and pleading of the Lord, longsuffering and merciful, at the end of His patience. Sorrowful and lamenting what He will do because they are a stiff-necked and gainsaying people. The same frustration Jesus felt, preaching to the Jews, 600yrs later.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

God says the punishment coming is due to their own wickedness, their bitter heart. Wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge. Their destruction is their own doing, and God laments this, as a husband would putting away his wife that he loves for her adultery.

Jeremiah sees visions of desolation, cities sacked and spoiled. The sky black from smoke. The fields, destroyed. Even the birds fleeing, for there are no men left.

And the Lord, who is a jealous God, asks what will Israel do when its destruction has come? He compares the nation to an old harlot. Decked in crimson, face caked with makeup, appealing to her lovers that she fornicated with, the other nations and their gods, and He says without Him. Without their land and riches. These lovers will turn and seek their lives. Without God they are vanity.

teachings.title: A remnant according to the election of grace
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: God saves or condemns by belief and unbelief, not ethnicity or nation: Israel's branches were broken off for unbelief, Gentiles are grafted in by faith, and God's children are Abraham's seed by faith.
teachings.text:
**2 Peter 3:9**
*The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.*

**Romans 11:1-5**
*I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.*

It is important to recognize that it isn't by ethnicity or nation that God saves or condemns, but by belief and unbelieving.

The destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel was for their unbelief. The eventual destruction of Judea was for rejecting Christ. At the end of the world, on that great and terrible day of the Lord, the wrath will come on the whole earth for unbelief, the righteous remnant spared, and Jesus will get rule with all His saints.

**Romans 11:15-21,30-32**
*For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.*.. *For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

The love of God is conditional on belief in His word. The Bible says, without faith it is impossible to please God. His children are children by faith, adopted as sons of God through Christ. Heirs according to His promise, made Abraham's seed for belief.

Those that remain in unbelief are cast into the fire by their own choice. By their own counsels.

teachings.title: Zion, the redeemed bride of Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zion and Jerusalem are a picture of the believer, the redeemed bride of Christ whom He jealously protects and will perfect as the New Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
But, Zion, like believers, stained crimson in sin, has a redeemer. And, like His church, Jerusalem is His bride, made perfect and decked in the finest array, fit for the King.

**Isaiah 61:10**
*I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.*

**Isaiah 62:1–7**
*For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth. And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name. Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God. Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee. I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.*

Zion, and Jerusalem, are a picture of the believer. A bride of Christ, made precious by His redemption, protecting it like a jealous husband;

**Zechariah 1:14**
*So the angel that communed with me said unto me, Cry thou, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.*

**Isaiah 54:5–7**
*For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. For the LORD hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God. For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.*

In the end, we shall see New Jerusalem, upon his holy hill, Zion. Perfected as a picture of his people, His bride;

**Revelation 21:1–2**
*And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.*

This is the promise of his holy place, how much more so is it the promise for those who have trusted in Christ. In an unmovable Rock, the cornerstone laid in Zion. The Rock of our salvation, we who are the bride of Christ. Amen

teachings.title: Mount Zion, chosen of God
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: Zion is holy because God placed His name there and separated it for His purposes, the place of Christ's sacrifice and future reign, not because its people are holy.
teachings.text:
Mount Zion, Jerusalem, is often referenced and praised as the place God chose to place His name. His holy city, the mountain providing natural protection on 3 sides, situated perfectly. A river running through the fertile valley. The setting where Abraham brought Issac. Where God prepared Himself a sacrifice. Where Jesus was slain and rose again, and where He will reign in the Kingdom to come.

The name, Zion, means a “monument; raised up; sepulcher,” the place of the tomb, hewn out of rock, the site of Christ's burial. Chosen by God.

Jerusalem, the city isn't a lonely peak, but rather a settlement nestled within a protective bowl of higher terrain, with Mt Moriah and the mount of Olives part of the limestone rings, defending the area.

**Psalm 125:1–2**
*They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever. As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.*

Beautiful for situation, a perfect location, the city if the great King on its north face.

**Psalm 132:13–14**
*For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.*

**1 Peter 2:5–6**
*Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.*

The shelter of Zion, the cornerstone of which is Christ, is where Jesus returns to in the end times, with the 144,000 witnesses.

**Revelation 14:1**
*And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.*

The defenses of this holy mountain were enough to dissuade kings and armies.

Sennacherib, of Assyria, the most powerful emperor of the ancient world, invaded Judah with a massive army of 185,000 soldiers.

He sent his top military commanders to the walls of Jerusalem, fiercely mocking King Hezekiah and blaspheming God, confidently expecting the city to fall just like every other nation before it.

Hezekiah called out to the Lord for protection of the city.

**2 Kings 19:16–19**
*LORD, bow down thine ear, and hear: open, LORD, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God. Of a truth, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands, And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art the LORD God, even thou only.*

And God harkened to the prayer, for His own purposes and will;

**2 Kings 19:32–34**
*Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.*

Zion is defended for His own sake, because He placed His name there, and for the promise made to David that out of Zion shall come a King.

**Romans 11:26–27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Zion is holy, because it has been separated unto the purposes of God.

It is not holy because the people there are holy. God allowed Babylon to raze the city and remove the people. Jesus decreed that Jerusalem would fall, and in 70AD it did. With the end times approaching, the city is considered wicked;

teachings.title: The inheritance belongs to all in Christ
teachings.theme: The church is the Israel of God
teachings.summary: The land promise is fulfilled in the resurrection and the inheritance passes to all who have put on Christ, so Christians who give it away to modern Zionism for politics are like Esau selling his birthright.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 8:7–10**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people*

The promise to occupy the land will be fulfilled for the Old Testament believers, in the resurrection. The only "Zionism" that matters is Christ Jesus on His throne. The inheritance is passed to all who have put on Christ.

**Romans 8:14–17**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together*.

This promise, the inheritance and blessings, is the heritage of all believers, from Adam and Abel, Seth and Noah, through every professing Christian today.

The spirit of Esau, who forsook his inheritance for a bowl of pottage, lives in Christians, who for political expediency seek to give it away.

**Hebrews 12:14–17**
*Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.*

This tearful repentance will be the case for many in the end times. Those who placed modern politics and bad theology above the joy unspeakable found in Jesus for all who believe, Jew or Gentile. Man or woman. Bond or free.

teachings.title: We have Abraham to our father
teachings.summary: The claim that the Jews inherit the land as Abraham's many children is the false basis of Zionism, since the promises were always conditional on obedience to God's covenant.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 33** concludes, the destruction of Jerusalem has happened. One who escaped comes to the prophet in the evening and tells him, but the hand of God keeps Ezekiel from responding until the morning came, and he was no longer struck dumb. And he receives the word of God.

The Lord says that those from the wastes and wilderness of Judah, who escaped out of the desolation of Jerusalem speak, saying that because Abraham was one, and was promised land, that they being many deserve the inheritance.

This is the argument made by Jews today. The basis of Zionism. The false doctrine that because they are children of the law, and many, the promise of the land given Abraham should apply even more so to them.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

The promises and inheritance was never given a people because of who they were. But by the condition of what they did. A condition repeatedly given.

**Exodus 19:5**
*Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine*

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The word of the Lord upon Ezekiel stresses these same points. They are filled with violence and Idolatry and adultery and abominations.

For this, God says He will lay the land most desolate because of their abominations. Then they shall know He is the Lord.

teachings.title: The promise was to Abraham's seed, which is Christ
teachings.summary: The promise to Abraham was made to his seed Christ and to all who are in Christ, the land promise was fulfilled under Joshua and kept conditionally under the Mosaic covenant, so Zionism wrongly gives the inheritance to unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 48** broadly captures the grandeur and love of God towards His holy land. This love is seen long before Israel as a nation enters in, or even exists. It was in the beginning, when God promised a land to Abraham.

**Genesis 12:1–3**
*Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.*

The promise to Abraham was both for the land, and the Christ. Long before the exodus. Long before the wandering. Before Isaac was ever born, the land that would become Israel, the province of Judah, the city of Jerusalem, in the mountains of Zion, was set apart for God.

The blessings and inheritance made to Abraham, who believed God and it was counted for righteousness, was made to him and his seed. Jesus Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Zionism is a modern political ideology that takes the promise to Abraham, and rather than give the inheritance and blessing to Christ, and all who are in Christ, gives it to unbelieving, apostate Jews.

**Galatians 3:27–29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The claim for the children of Israel to the land, by promise of God, was fulfilled in the time of Joshua.

**Joshua 21:43–45**
*And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein. And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand. There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.*

The promise to Abraham was unconditional. But the promise made to Moses by God in the wilderness, for His people to occupy His land, was conditional.

**Deuteronomy 28:63–64**
*And it shall come to pass, that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. And the LORD shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.*

Many Christians today will say "God keeps His promises! The Jews deserve this land!" They place political Zionism and the ethnic ultranationalism of the modern Jewish state as being part of an unconditional and irrevocable covenant with the people by heritage and genealogy.

But the Bible is clear, that the covenant made in the wilderness was explicitly conditional, that what was given to the people through Moses could not, by their failure, disannul the promise made to Abraham and his singular seed.

**Galatians 3:17–18**
*And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.*

But the covenant made those 430 years after Abraham? It has faded away, replace by a better covenant with better promises, to all who are in Christ, regardless of their ethnicity or origin.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Jerusalem as dross
teachings.summary: Jerusalem broke the old covenant through idolatry, false prophets and oppressing the poor, despised God's longsuffering, and was judged and cast out like dross, which is why a new covenant was needed.
teachings.text:
We see here in the preaching against Jerusalem, where the Lord demands the prophet tell the Jews of their abominations and His judgment, that much of it mirrors those things given to Moses in the wilderness. The things God proclaimed should be dealt with by death. That the blood be upon the wicked and not on the people in the land.

But the children of Israel failed to uphold their end of the covenant and now faced the promised judgment.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I Made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The longsuffering of God, that nearly 1,000 years passed from Sinai and the law to the utter destruction of Jerusalem, was taken by the people to mean God wasn't present. That He no longer cared. That maybe He wasn't real.

His mercy and calls to repentance, ignored. The grace He offers men because of His love, taken advantage of. For greed and lust.

And false prophets preaching lies, saying "The Lord has spoken," when He hadn't. And devouring widow's houses and taking advantage of the poor and the fatherless.

**Matthew 23:13-15**
*But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves*.

The Lord looked for the righteous to be the salt that preserves, and found none. Just like in Sodom, where He told Moses if there were found just 10 righteous men, He would spare the cities. And so He promises to gather the wicked and melt them in flame like the molten metals they make their abominations with. For sacrifice in the mountains. For their idolatry, for their shedding of blood. For their degeneracy. Extortion, usury, greed.

They have become as dross. Impurities in the silver, cast out.

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: the unbelieving Jews rejected
teachings.summary: He teaches that Paul frames Jewish persecution as reprobate versus elect, that per Jeremiah 6:30 the unbelieving Jews are rejected of God while saved Greek and Jew are now His elect, and that Jewish antichrists are turned over to a reprobate mind.
teachings.text:
Paul is again writing of the reprobate, the rejected of God, and those abominable and disobedient deceivers going after the *elect*, or chosen.

When Paul frequently writes of the Jewish persecution of the faithful, he frames it in terms of the reprobate vs the elect, because he is trying to show the Gentiles that THEY are the chosen people of God now, and the Jews the rejected:

"*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them."* **Jeremiah 6:30**

This deliberate use is misinterpreted by calvanists who miss the point being made; that Saved Christians, "Greek and Jew" are now God's chosen, His elect, not the unbelieving Jew. And that they in their jealousy and envy, have further become filled with all unrighteousness.

To be a Jew of the flesh after the coming of Christ is to reject God. To not retain Him in their knowledge. Jews whole identity is that rejection, and God's reprobation of them in return.

This is why Jewish antichrists are so wicked. They are turned over to a reprobate mind.

teachings.title: Romans 11 and the reprobate nation of Israel
teachings.summary: Paul's argument in Romans 11 is that the remnant are those Jews who believe the Gospel, and that God does not hold out salvation indefinitely but cuts off the unbelieving, whether individuals or a nation, and turns them over to reprobation.
teachings.text:
Here in Romans 11, Paul is finishing the JQ begun in chapter 9 and 10, as it pertains to Israel after the flesh, the nation, now that Christ had come.

This builds on the theme he has from the start; that all men are without excuse in condemnation, and further some men and nations condemn themselves by bringing God to reject them utterly, unto reprobation. That even with the law, the Jews were condemned and without it, so were the Gentiles. That the Gospel of faith alone in grace alone of the resurrection, into His kingdom, was the promise that faith was placed in. Without works. *To him that worketh not.* That this election of grace applies to the Gentile as much as the Jew. That there is no difference between Jew and the Greek, that if all are condemned, then all are saved in Jesus if they believe. It's flawless doctrine, relentlessly building on itself.

Here in Romans 11 Paul is finishing the thought of what to say about the physical Israel, the Jews, given all this doctrine. What does the Gospel of Christ mean pertaining to the old covenant? (God is a logical God, who wants us to *reason together* with Him)

Dispensationalism rests primarily on vs 1-5, and, like most bad doctrine, isolating verses out of context to achieve it. They say "see, God's not done with Israel!"

But here Paul specifically is offering himself as the example, that the remnant is those who believe the Gospel. For we know from the prior chapters that there is a conditional state to salvation, belief. Obeying the Gospel. And so any Jew who believes will be that remnant. Same as the Greek who are grafted in to the promise by their faith.

Verse 6 has God hammer again the point that salvation is not by works. It is 100% by faith, least it no more be of grace. Because it is a gift and the rewards for work is a debt owed. (Works-nibbas BTHO, again)

So, having established that the Jews after the flesh have to believe, Paul circles back to Romans 1 and reprobate doctrine, calling in mind the imprecatory prayer of David to blind the wicked who reject the truth of God, unto damnation.

However, Paul prays that the Gentiles receiving the blessing and promises, being grafted in, provoked his kinsmen to repentance. That they turn from stubborn unbelief to accepting the Gospel. That they who are believe would be sent, preaching the word, and by hearing, physical Israel believe and be grafted in again. That by his own example living for Christ he gets his nation to want to emulate him and be saved.

This plea is a familiar lament to many Christians. We all have unsaved relatives, often close. Friends, coworkers. People for whom we earnestly pray accept the free gift of salvation but who have hardened their hearts.

Paul's example of being worthy of emulation is a model for us, that we live the Gospel in a way that draws them to the light and softens their hearts that they may be willing to believe.

The warning to Gentiles against becoming arrogant regarding their position relative to grace and the reprobate silver nation of Jews should also be taken to heart.

A Godly nation can easily turn from the truth and be burned in the fire, just as easily as recalcitrant Israel could have a revival in Christ and be graft back in. Prodigals restored as heirs.

Dispies falsely make this an unconditional statement rather than an argument; that Jews **will** be graft in regardless of their own belief or wickedness.

Paul has built his case, in the Spirit, that everything here is contingent on believing God's law and promises, whom all men know, and knowing are condemned without excuse, except they believe in the gospel, which is of faith in Christ's crucifixion and resurrection for the remission of all sins, that this is a gift available to everyone, without works, entirely of grace, but that God doesn't hold it out to be taken indefinitely, and that at some point He will cut off the unbelieving, reject and turn them over to reprobation. Individual salvation to eternal life, or a physical nation on earth, it's the same.

teachings.title: The wicked husbandmen given over
teachings.summary: In the parable of the vineyard Jesus shows the Jews who knew the truth yet sought to kill Him, so God gave them over to a reprobate mind and will destroy them and give the kingdom to others, contrary to dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
Following the story of the fig tree which Jesus cursed for not producing fruit, He tells a parable. The master leaving a vineyard to be tended sends for the gathering, and the husbandmen he'd entrusted with the land beat and kill his messengers. He sends his only begotten son and they plot to kill him and take the inheritance for themselves.

With this not so thinly veiled analogy, Jesus puts the Jews who are seeking to kill Him on notice. They discern that Jesus is talking about them. Unlike most of His parables that fell on deaf ears. The Bible says "*they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way*."

It is amazing to us who believe that there are those who knowing the truth, seek to silence it, even with the Son of the Lord standing there in their presence. Even with the history of the Jews, who killed the prophets of God, and now plot to do the same to Christ.

They wish to not retain the word of God and the truth of Christ in their knowledge. They sought instead to take the inheritance of an earthly kingdom for themselves by His death. They worship the creation more than the creator. And God turned them over, gave them up, to a reprobate mind to do those things which are inconvenient.

*Reprobate silver men shall call them.*

Again, the dispensationalist idea that the Jews held a special place and God wasn't through with them yet, is a lie. They were given the advantage of the oracles of God and the ministry of Jesus Christ in the flesh, and rather than repent towards God, they sought to destroy Him.

And like the master of the vineyard, *he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.*

It does not say He will take it from them for a time. He destroys them and gives the Kingdom to those who will produce fruit, giving God the increase, in His Son's name.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: a national identity
teachings.summary: Quoting Romans 1:18-32 and Jeremiah 6:30, he teaches that the Jews who rejected the Messiah are reprobate by their individual free will and collectively judged, so that it is their national identity.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-32**

*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,*
*And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*
*Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

*For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*
*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

Speaking specifically of the Jews who would reject the coming Messiah;

**Jeremiah 6:30**

*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

It is their national identity. By their individual free will. Collectively judged.

teachings.title: Righteousness by faith, not circumcision
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before circumcision, so no rite, baptism, or work is required for salvation, and the inheritance is by faith in Christ, not by fleshly descent as Zionism and dispensationalism claim.
teachings.text:
So this is the promise made by God that if we believe on the Son, we are saved by His grace. Our sins forgiven. No sin even being imputed upon us. Whether we work or not, because work is debt not grace.

Paul continues using Abraham's example;

*Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.*

Abraham did not receive the ordinance of circumcision until decades after his believing God's promise, and being saved by that faith. He was blessed with the accounting of righteousness when he did not know circumcision. So this promise, predating this rite of the Jews, means it does not only apply to the circumcised, but also to the uncircumcised. And so the promise of grace doesn't require circumcision, but faith alone.

This point is both specific to the issue of circumcision being introduced by the Judaizers in Paul's day, but also generally speaking, that there is no rite or ordinance that is required for salvation. Not baptism. Not any ritual or keeping of tradition. No works of the law.

*And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also*.

Abraham as the father of all who believe, the circumcision of the spirit, the generation of believers are partakers of the promise, that the righteousness of God is imputed upon us in faith.

*For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.*

The promise of God that Abraham believed was that through his faith, he would be made father to many nations, and inherit the kingdom of God. This promise was made possible in Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

Unbelieving Jews felt they were owed the kingdom by God for being Abraham's seed under the law. That the inheritance was by blood, and the promise made to them after the flesh, and not in the spirit.

This is the basis for Zionism and the false doctrine of dispensationalism.

But the Bible teaches the exact opposite. There is no difference between Jew and Gentile. All are under sin. It is by faith only that we are made heirs. That the seed of the promise is Christ manifest in the flesh.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It is not an inheritance by the law but by faith. Like Esua and Jacob, the inheritance went to the younger. It was taken from the elder, who with tears sought repentance from God, but none was found.

**Luke 13:25-30**
*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.*

teachings.title: Modern Jews as reprobate silver
teachings.summary: Modern Jews are not the descendants of the twelve tribes but a people defined by rejecting Jesus, given up and cursed by God as reprobate silver, which undoes the dispensationalist hope for their salvation.
teachings.text:
Before getting back into the chapter itself, I want to reiterate that whatever else they are, Modern Jews are not the sons of Judah from the Old Testament.

Whether they are Edomites or Khazarians, or some other people, regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story and Jewish fables, We know they are not the descendants of the 12 tribes of Israel. To the extent they may have some of Abraham's blood in them, So does most of the world.

The one defining characteristic of all modern Jews, and by modern I mean going back to the first few centuries AD, or the foundation of Judaism 400 years after Christ, all Jews hold as their primary identity the rejection of Jesus. Be they Ashkenazi, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, Reformed, orthodox, atheist, conservative or liberal... Every single Jew is an antichrist. And God will make of them a synagogue of Satan.

Reprobate silver will men call them. For they have been given up and rejected by God.

I make this caveat because as we know, dispensationalism is about modern Jews, not the 12 tribes of Israel which no longer exist and haven't existed since 70 AD.

When they say that they think that God isn't finished with the Jews or that all the Jews will end up being saved at the second coming of Christ, they are talking about this reprobate group that the Bible says aren't actually Jews. They aren't even Israel after the flesh let alone spiritual Israel, which are all believers.

And God has cursed them.

teachings.title: No plan B for the cut off
teachings.summary: From Romans 11 he teaches that those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate, and that doubting this by imagining a secret plan to win them back questions the judgment of God.
teachings.text:
And so, *As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes.*

God would that they believe and be saved. He would glory in the older being brought back into the Kingdom with the younger. But it can only happen through faith, and those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate.

*For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

It's all about faith. We are all in sin and grace is offered all of us.

*O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

Many find it unfair that some are cut off, they refuse to believe the Reprobate Doctrine, they doubt the judgment of God. They think He must have some secret plan to win them back. A plan B. But the only plan is Christ. And Him crucified. And it is not for us to question the judgment and mercy of God. He will have mercy on whom He has mercy. It's not up to us to tell Him, but to humbly submit to His will.

*For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Judah rejected
teachings.summary: From Jeremiah 6 he teaches that Judah, with its false prophets crying peace, was rejected of God as reprobate silver, and that God judges nations the same way today, especially those called by His name.
teachings.text:
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace....Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

Jeremiah, in the Spirit, is preaching hard against Judah, which has become totally corrupt, and faces judgment from the North, by the invading armies of Babylon which God is warning He will allow to conquer and spoil them.

And the prophets and priests are telling the people "Peace. Peace" when there is no peace. They speak soothing words, withholding judgement, leaving the people with a false sense of security. That everything is fine.

That their sacrifices and their expensive, imported incense, the performative religious acts they do, will offset the Idolatry, fornication and wickedness.

Jeremiah preaches that this is not acceptable to the Lord and they will be spoiled and left desolate. Reprobate, rejected by God.

A millennium after God takes the children out of Israel, clearing the land of the nations that committed  abominations, driving then out before them, and here they sit facing the same judgment. The northern kingdom of 10 tribes, wiped out and dispersed by the Assyrians, and Judah about to be overrun by Babylonians. And despite the warnings of the prophet, none of them repent of their ways. They break the covenant and despite God's longsuffering, His wrath is upon them.

How can we not help but see the parallels and understand we face the same judgment?

God judges nations by their works, and especially by those who call themselves by His name. If those claiming Him, who say they are Israel, fall away, He is going to cut them off.

It is a real 🎯 you are here-moment.

teachings.title: God is a God of separation
teachings.summary: From creation onward God separates and divides to make a holy people, separating believing Israel after the Spirit from unbelieving Israel after the flesh, wheat from chaff, until the harvest is complete.
teachings.text:
Here we go.

God is a God of separation. The Bible has example after example of division, separating one thing from another. Day from night. The creatures after their own kind. Woman from man. Man from the Garden. Cain and Abel. The descendents of Seth, the sons of God that called upon the name of the Lord and the children of men who did not. Noah and his perfect generations from fallen man. The animals of the ark. The nations of Noah's sons. The people of Babel and their languages. The habitations of the nations. Abraham out of Ur. Ishmael and Isaac. Jacob and Esau. Joseph and his brothers. Hebrews out of their land and into Egypt. Out of Egypt and back in the land. The covenant with Moses that they would be a holy people. Separated from other nations.

Even here, in Numbers, each tribe separated and counted. And the Levites separated even further.

**Luke 12:51**
*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:*

The division. The separation. Making holy a people of God. Separating Israel from Judah. And Jesus from the root of Jesse. Believing Israel from the non-believing Jews. The tares from the wheat. Sheep from goats. Israel after the flesh and Israel after the Spirit. Unfruitful branches cut off and cast into the fire. The election in Christ chosen to be graft in.

**Deuteronomy 7:6**
*For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.*

**Isaiah 62:12**
*And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.*

**1 Peter 2:9**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light;*

Winnowing the chaff from the wheat. The earth is His threshing floor. The harvest is ongoing. We are in the last days, and have been since the first fruit of Christ, and the harvest of 5,000 made by the disciples on Pentecost. We shall bring in the sheaves for the Lord. To Him the increase. Until the fullness of the harvest comes in.

Amen

teachings.title: Israel a reprobate nation
teachings.summary: From Hosea 4 he teaches that Israel, not wishing to retain God in its knowledge, was given over as a reprobate nation to be consumed by its sins, the same judgment coming on the world.
teachings.text:
Continuing the preaching against Israel, its people are wicked, especially even their priests, those low men that were established by Jeroboam, when he introduced idolatry to the people and caused all Israel to sin.

Hosea preaches hard against their sins; the violence and bloodshed, the drunkenness, the literal whoredoms and adultery, and spiritual; chasing after false gods.

The Lord says that if they don't wish to retain Him in their knowledge, they will perish for that lack of knowledge. If the priests won't reprove and rebuke sin, then they are in common cause with it. Let their sins consume them. God won't even scourge them for backsliding. They've been given up and given over, a reprobate nation.

They go to the stocks for advice, that is to wooden idols, sacrifices in groves, seeking favor of their dead gods. So the living God says let their daughters and wives go whoring as they have to Him.

What a wicked time, and the destruction of Israel was long past due. Only the longsuffering love of the Lord stayed their end.

The Lord does make provision to keep the evil out of Judah, that the false religion and fornications of the North, the Idolatry of Ephraim, would not spread into the Southern Kingdom, for now.

What a condemnation. And it is the same righteous judgement of God that will be passed on to the world, even as Judah, or that is saved Christians today, are spared. It may seem like the wicked prosper and go unpunished, but as we see here, that is a punishment in itself. Allowing the blood to heap against them, their own sins to make them miserable, even as they compound. And then, destruction.

Perfect is the judgment of God

teachings.title: I am the LORD, there is none else
teachings.summary: God's specific prophecy of Cyrus proves He alone is God and that His promise of salvation in Christ is just as sure, and the Israel that shall be saved is all who are Abraham's seed by faith in Christ.
teachings.text:
Continuing the very clear, undeniable, easy to understand prophecy of God through Isaiah, of the future King of the Medo-Persian empire, more than a century off in the future. **Isaiah 45** is one of the most powerful chapters in the Bible.

God says He has named Cyrus as deliverer, for after the Babylonian captivity, still decades away, after the 70 years of desolation in Jerusalem as prophesied, the Babylonian empire will be over thrown, and Cyrus will free the Jews wot return, to rebuild the temple. That the line of David continued to Christ and the place God put His name would stand until it served its purpose, the death burial and resurrection of Jesus.

And just as sure and specific and certain as this prophecy is for Cyrus, so it is for the Messiah.

By this we may know there is no other God beside Him. He is the Lord, and there is none else.

For all creation testifies, and all the prophets gave witness, and all the promises made to the faithful, and the evidence all around that those who trust in Him are never ashamed.

God calls all His shots beforehand, and we see the results are true. And if these things are sure and true, then know the promise of salvation and eternal life in Christ Jesus is as well.

*Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the Lord have created it.*

The Lord has created all things that, in His time, in the end, salvation and righteousness are as a flood upon the earth. And like the flood of Noah, we shall be delivered and those that reject God will be destroyed.

Those that chase after gods of their own hands, who worship the created more than the Creator, shall be confounded and ashamed when the day comes.

*But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.*

The Lord openly declares these things, all that is right. His perfect law. His kept promises. His holy Name.

*I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.*

**John 5:37**
*And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.*

**Philippians 2:9-11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father*

**1 John 5:7**
*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

The word of God is true, let every man be a liar who rejects it. All that are incensed against Him shall be ashamed. Those who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge, who hold the truth in unrighteousness, they will be made to know He loves us.

And in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and glory.

**Galatians 3:27-29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

**Romans 11:26-27**
*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Amen

teachings.title: Statutes that were not good
teachings.summary: In Ezekiel 20 God gave idolatrous Israel and Judah over to strong delusion and statutes that were not good, as Romans 1 describes, while still pleading with their hardened hearts and promising the kingdom to come.
teachings.text:
This cycle continued, and in Judah as well. *Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live*.

He gave them over to strong delusion, that they may believe a lie. He allowed them to see what happens when they trusted their own foolish hearts that were darkened.

**Romans 1:21-25**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

They went to the high places, Bamah in Hebrew, instead of the mount of the Lord, the Temple of Zion in Jerusalem. They worshiped idols in His name and offered sacrifice to them, and ultimately passed their own sons through the fire to Baal. Even those that sat down to enquire of the Lord this day.

*Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations?*

God pleads with them as He did with their fathers, that His word against them would prick them in their hardened hearts. That they turn from the sins of their father to embrace the truth of the Lord God.

To that end, He says He will put them to the rod. And destruction and desolation. That He will purge the unrighteous from among them. But if they repented not, so be it. The Lord asks one thing of them, stop doing their gifts and offerings and abominations to their idols in HIS holy name.

*For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things.*

This isn't only the restoration of Jerusalem after the captivity. But a prophecy of what would come.

This is the Kingdom of Heaven. This is the holy reign of Christ. This is the final assembly of believers, who will be sanctified before the heathen for His holy name, Jesus. And we shall know that He is the Lord.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple: a promise on condition
teachings.summary: The temple vision was a conditional promise to Israel of Christ and a kingdom if they repented, which they refused, as Christ lamented over Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
Ezekiel is no different. It is the explicit purpose of the Temple prophecy, giving the people a promise, contingent on their getting right:

**Ezekiel 43:10-11** 
*Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them*.

The promises given the people included Christ, and a Kingdom, if they repented towards the Law and God.

**Zachariah 6:12-15**
*Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is* The Branch*; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the Lord. And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the Lord, and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God.*

They could be children of the Kingdom if they were ashamed of their abominations, took the chastening God consistently gave them, and like the heathen of Nineveh, turned from the wicked ways,

God sent prophets, and they killed them. God wiped out the Northern Kingdom as an example. He brings Judah into bondage under Babylon, and makes His holy city desolate. All to goad them to come to repentance that they would be His people, and He would be their God.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

teachings.title: Thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter
teachings.summary: Zechariah 11 prophesies judgment on Judah's false shepherds and the breaking of the covenant, and his price of thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter is fulfilled in Judas' betrayal of the Good Shepherd.
teachings.text:
Continuing in Zechariah, we see the prophet turn from active encouragement in previous chapters to a more negative message and future prophecy against Judah.

The doors of Lebanon, the cedars, the oaks of Bashan, which is the fertile eastern bank of the Jordan, these represent the built temple, the great city Jerusalem, forged by the timber from these areas. Zechariah is prophesying their destruction, when reconstruction has hardly even begun.

The leaders, the shepherds, howl at their loss, the young lions roar, because the pride of Jordan is spoiled by false teachers and bad leadership at the judgment of God against them.

These wicked leaders, God says, slay the people and hold themselves not guilty. They sell them into servitude and think they are bless by the riches that comes to them for the price of men. The shepherds have no pity for their flock.

And God says this is His judgement on the Jews. Sort of the flip side of **Jeremiah 3:15**

*And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding*.

So, Zechariah preaches the destruction of the people at the hands of their neighbors and the kings and the Lord will not deliver them as He has so many times. As He just had from captivity. This is a future event.

God will feed the flock to the slaughter.

This all could be a prophecy of 70AD and the destruction of Jerusalem. The temple, as Christ said would come. Not on stone standing upon another. The scattering and spoil of the pride of the Jordan. The burning of the cedars and oaks. Or dual fulfilment with the days of vengeance, the end times prophecy of the destruction of Israel.

**Luke 21:21-22**
*Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

The prophet takes up two shepherd staves, and on one staff he writes "Beauty" and the other is called "Bands."

He says three shepherds he cut off in one month, and that he hated them and they hated him. False teachers, it seems. I can't say if this is Zechariah rebuking them, and taking their followers away from them, or God speaking directly that He did this to them. Either way, the flock of Judah is then cut off.

He breaks the staff "Beauty," which is the covenant with the people. Note the poor of the flock who believed on Him knew this was the word of the Lord. As a prophecy of Christ, and the new covenant that was established, the poor knew Jesus was the Word of the Lord.

Then he asks the people for his price as shepherd, and they set it at 30 pieces of silver. The parallel is obvious.

**Matthew 26:14-15**
*Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver*.

The good Shepherd, valued at only a lowly sum, 30 pieces of silver to be betrayed. And says to cast the sum to the potter.

**Matthew 27:3-7**
*Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in.*

The act of throwing the money to the potter was a symbolic rejection in Zechariah, and the purchase of the potter's field with the money is the fulfilment.
